messages:
maya: quick heads-up — noticed quota attribution jumping around for some legacy API keys after the edge proxy roll last night.
connor: seen it too. repro steps?
maya: curl hits endpoint with api-key, but when proxied through our rate-limiter we seem to drop the project claim.
maya: example request:
```
curl -H "Authorization: ApiKey abc123" -H "X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
kiara: is this the header rewriting bug we saw in alpha? edge was removing X-Redwood-Project in 2.1.4
connor: looks like that. Edge 2.1.4 introduced route normalization that strips unknown X- headers unless whitelisted.
sam: so attribution falls back to token's org claim which for some legacy keys is org-level, hence billing to wrong project.
maya: yeah. Two concrete asks: (1) telemetry to pin per-request effective_project in console so customers can debug; (2) a rollout plan to restore attribution without breaking proxies.
kiara: for telemetry, we can add a computed field `effective_project` in request logs and surface as a column in per-route dashboard. sampling 1% initially?
connor: 1% good. also add a tag `auth_source` = [token_claim, header, exchange].
maya: UI note — console should show both `requested_project` and `effective_project` and a tooltip explaining fallthrough order.
sam: +1. What about quick mitigation? reconfigure edge to whitelist X-Redwood-Project for 24h and patch 2.1.5.
connor: can do. patch will re-emit claim from token if header absent instead of clearing claim.
kiara: need a canary: deploy to us-east edge pool at 10% traffic for 6h, watch ratio of effective_project != requested_project.
deploy-bot: deploy request created: /deploy edge-whitelist-2.1.5 canary 10% us-east by connor — CI passed.
maya: I'll own console change — will add column and a compact explanation. Kiara can own logging + schema change to add auth_source.
kiara: schema change: add string field `auth_source` to request_logs v2. Need migration note for downstream metrics.
sam: billing implications — finance wants a rollforward plan if we retroactively attribute. We should avoid retroactive rebilling.
maya: agreed — we only change visibility, not historical billing. Ops: disable any retroactive aggregation jobs.
connor: timeline: edge patch today, canary 10% for 6h, if green expand to 100% over 3 hours. telemetry 1% live right away, console column behind a feature flag.
sam: communicate to support: short blurb for impacted customers and how to interpret console fields.
maya: draft message for support: "If you see mismatched effective_project, it's because legacy keys lack project claim and edge dropped forwarded header — we're rolling a fix and adding visibility." I'll post in #support when canary starts.
kiara: one more: ensure rate-limit keys continue to match routing precedence. Proposed precedence in config:
```
auth.routing.precedence = [
  "token_claim.project",
  "x-redwood-project",
  "x-origin-project",
  "fallback:org"
]
```
connor: minor change: move header checks above token_claim for proxied traffic? that might break clients behind proxies. Let's keep token_claim first.
sam: ok. final ask: add an automated alert if >0.5% of requests have effective_project != requested_project after canary expands.
deploy-bot: alert created: auth.attribution.mismatch > 0.5% 5m.
maya: thanks team — I'll circle back after canary results.
connor: TY, will monitor logs and post metrics link.
sam: ping me when the support note is ready.
kiara: will open PR for log schema now.
maya: (edited) created console PR: link-to-pr.dev/123 — feature flag `show_effective_project`.
sam: :thumbsup:
